## Motivation

DSA-style sparse attention (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V4.1) picks the top-k keys of every prefill row from an indexer score over all visible keys. Today this is DeepGEMM `mqa_logits` writing the full `[rows, keys]` logits, then a separate top-k over them. At long context both the logits traffic and the top-k grow with `rows x keys`.

This PR adds an opt-in sampled-threshold path (after [LiteTopK](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976), building on #46434): one SM100 kernel scores every key on the tensor cores and keeps only the keys at or above a per-row threshold taken from a strided sample of the row's scores (about 2.25 x topk candidates per row), then a small top-k selects among the candidates. The logits are never written.

## Changes

- Kernels (`kernels/jit/csrc/dsa/litetopk_prefill/`): FP8 indexer (DSA, 32/64 index heads), FP4 indexer (DeepSeek-V4.1, 32/64 index heads), fp32 / bf16 candidate top-k (topk 512 / 1024 / 2048); `attention/topk_page_table_transform.cuh` maps request-relative positions to KV slots through the page-size-64 table (PAGED output).
- Ops: `attention.fp8_indexer_topk`, `attention.fp4_indexer_topk`, `attention.topk_page_table_transform_`.
- Integration behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_PREFILL_LITE_TOPK=1` (default off):
  - DSA prefill (RAGGED and PAGED / trtllm outputs) when the batch's longest row sees at least `8 x index_topk` keys.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1 full top-k layers when the batch's longest request has at least 24576 compressed keys.
  - Shorter batches keep the dense path.
- First commit: a refactor of the `sgl_kernel` PTX helpers into `sgl_kernel/ptx/{barrier,async,tcgen05}.cuh` (shared by the new kernels and the existing wo_a / kimi attn_res / hicache / muse kernels), plus packed fp32x2 math helpers.
- Requires nvcc >= 13.4 for the JIT kernels.

## Kernel performance (B300, cold L2, indexer + top-k, us; ratio = baseline / ours)

FP8, 32 heads, topk 2048 (single request, last rows), vs DeepGEMM fp8 logits + DeepSelect:

| context x rows | ours | DeepGEMM + DeepSelect | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32K x 4096 | 482 | 1181 | 2.45 |
| 128K x 4096 | 1533 | 3307 | 2.16 |
| 256K x 8192 | 5932 | 11733 | 1.98 |
| 1M x 4096 | 11881 | 18732 | 1.58 |
| 1M x 16384 | 50161 | 84329 | 1.68 |

FP4, DeepSeek-V4.1 shapes (compress ratio 2, topk 512), vs DeepGEMM bf16 logits + DeepSelect:

| context x rows | keys | ours | DG + DS | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64K x 4096 (32 heads) | 32K | 397 | 459 | 1.16 |
| 256K x 16384 (32 heads) | 128K | 5182 | 5919 | 1.14 |
| 1M x 16384 (32 heads) | 512K | 20078 | 22477 | 1.12 |
| 256K x 16384 (64 heads) | 128K | 9095 | 9380 | 1.03 |

Below ~16K keys the filter keeps most keys and DeepGEMM + top-k is as fast or faster, hence the routing thresholds above.

## End-to-end (GLM-5.3 FP8, 8x B300, cookbook TP8 + EAGLE, trtllm prefill)

| workload | off | on | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| single 128K request, TTFT | 6690 ms | 5837 ms | -12.7% |
| single 64K request, TTFT | 2929 ms | 2761 ms | -5.7% |
| 128K x concurrency 4, input tok/s | 19942 | 23436 | +17.5% |
| 8K / 16K single request | | | within noise |

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (4x B200 TP4/EP4; AgentX screens on B300): within noise, since only 3 layers use the full top-k indexer.

## Correctness

- Unit tests (`test_dsa_prefill_{fp8_indexer,fp4_indexer,topk_candidates}.py`, `test_topk_page_table_transform.py`): FP8 / FP4 scores are bitwise equal to DeepGEMM's logits, candidate sets match `logits >= T`, and the final indices are the exact top-k up to ties.
- In-server comparison with the dense path on every prefill row (fresh, prefix-cached, chunked 128K and batched requests):
  - GLM-5.3: 41M rows, 99.9% identical, mean recall 0.9999995; the rest are near-tie swaps at rank ~2048.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: 2.3M rows, mean recall 0.994; all disagreements are copies of the k-th value (bf16 ties).
  - 0 out-of-range / duplicate indices, 0 overflow. About 1e-6 to 1e-5 of rows return a few fewer than k indices when the sampled threshold lands above the k-th score.
- Accuracy (sgl-eval 0.1.3, off / on):
  - GLM-5.3: ruler2 128K 87.27 / 87.69.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: gsm8k 96.66 / 96.89; ruler2 128K 82.17 / 79.68, paired difference not significant (p = 0.39).

Validated on B200 and B300.

Hi Ziyi, I tried a few changes on top of this PR (B200, nvcc 13.4.92, real GLM-5.2 dumps), with no fallback and no bigger slab. Ratios are kernel time against this PR; lower is faster.

**1. Sample single keys instead of 8-key blocks (the important one).** Top keys sit in runs, so an 8-key block either lands in one or misses it, and Threshold gets noisy. At about 1M keys some rows clip at `FP8_INDEXER_CAP`, unreported because the serving path doesn't read `overflow`, and some come back short. The change is single keys on an odd stride chosen from each block's span (65 up to 524288 keys, 129 up to 1M), loaded through a strided tensor map with one TMA call per tile, plus alpha 4.5 instead of 5.
- Correctness: 12 wrong rows (8 distinct, all on one 1M prompt) go to 0, out of 562,149 rows checked against fp64. Max candidates go from 13658 to 8620.
- Speed: 0.94 and 0.91 on layer 0 at 24K and 32K, 0.99-1.04 on later layers at 24K-32K, a tie from 64K up, including 1M.
- Trade-off: exact-copy keys whose period equals the stride resonate (64K keys, period 65: 14 to 3426 wrong rows). The 4 real files I checked have no bit-identical keys.

**2. Dynamic block claim in the FP8 indexer**, like the FP4 `BlockProducer`. Geomean 0.92 on 30 mixed chunks, a tie on single requests, 1.07 on the worst mix found.

**3. Page-table lookup inside the top-k gather**, so no transform launch. 0.97 at 24K, 0.98 at 64K, a tie at 1M.

All three together: 0.88 on layer 0 at 24K-32K, 0.94-1.00 on later layers at 24K-32K, a tie at 1M, 0.73 on a mixed 512K + 8 x 32K chunk.

In the end, thanks to your great contribution to Litetopk!

Best,
Ziqi

Thanks Ziqi, this was very helpful.

**1. Single-key sampling:** adopted in 24e21ed8ae for both indexers. Samples are single keys on an odd stride chosen from the block span (65 / 129 / 257 for FP8; 33 up to 48K keys of span, then 65-257 for FP4), with a hashed phase and one strided 3D TMA per sample tile. Alpha is 4 for FP8 and 4.5 for FP4. Validated on B300 with real GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill inputs up to 1M tokens:
- FP8: short rows 2 -> 0 (1.07M rows), max candidates 10720 -> 8422, kernel time 0.90-1.00x of the previous version.
- FP4: it had the same issue (short rows at ~500K compressed keys); short rows 12 -> 0, max candidates 5736 -> 4568, 0.96-1.00x.
- The per-key scale loads turned out cheap: removing them entirely saves under 1%.

**2. Dynamic block claim for FP8:** not in this PR; we may pick it up in a follow-up.

**3. Page-table lookup inside the top-k gather:** we'd prefer to keep the transform as a separate step, so the top-k stays independent of the KV layout.

Independent GB300 measurements on commit `599923b6f48d638d2256abbd0550c8fde141f4f5` (unmodified PR source). I measured the complete indexer + selection path, model-level TTFT and cold JIT compilation. The serving comparison below uses the same PR commit, toggling only `SGLANG_OPT_USE_PREFILL_LITE_TOPK`.

At 1,000,000 input tokens / concurrency 1, GLM-5.2-FP8 TTFT is **129.57 → 63.33 s (2.046×, 51.1% lower)**. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is **14.07 → 13.57 s (1.037×)**. The FP8 indexer module takes about **9.2 s** to compile/load cold; the separate cold medians for indexer plus candidate selector sum to about **15.5 s**, excluding other startup work.

### Environment and comparison

- 8× NVIDIA GB300 (SM103), two exclusive 4-GPU nodes. Kernel/JIT measurements use one GPU; serving uses TP8 across both nodes. GPU clocks were not locked by this benchmark.
- Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, nvcc/CUDA runtime headers 13.4.92, driver 590.48.01; FlashInfer 0.7.2, DeepGEMM 0.2.3.post2, sgl-kernel 0.4.10, TVM FFI 0.1.11. `MAX_JOBS=8`.
- For the **operator microbenchmarks**, the FP8 baseline is **DeepGEMM + the existing top-k v2**, not only DeepSelect; the FP4 baseline is DeepGEMM BF16 logits + DeepSelect. Both include score generation and selection. Serving uses the actual runtime dispatch described below.

### Complete indexer + top-k

32 index heads, 4,096 query rows (last causal chunk), head dimension 128. FP8: k=2048. FP4: k=512, compression ratio 2, so the number of keys is half the original context length. Times below are microseconds; speedup = baseline / LiteTopK.

| Original context | FP8 baseline → LiteTopK | Speedup | FP4 baseline → LiteTopK | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K | 185.98 → 300.70 | 0.62× | 83.58 → 72.35 | 1.16× |
| 32K | 656.00 → 457.34 | 1.43× | 234.14 → 215.74 | 1.09× |
| 64K | 1217.12 → 772.74 | 1.58× | 417.44 → 378.53 | 1.10× |
| 256K | 4861.60 → 3104.42 | 1.57× | 1446.59 → 1293.98 | 1.12× |
| 1M | 19783.33 → 12409.54 | 1.59× | 5481.12 → 4881.06 | 1.12× |

At 1M context / 16,384 query rows, FP8 is **79.62 → 49.59 ms (1.61×)** and FP4 is **21.14 → 18.90 ms (1.12×)**. The direct FP8 op is slower at 8K, but the production dispatch guard excludes that shape.

Baseline choice matters: for FP8 32K × 4096, DeepGEMM + DeepSelect takes 1065.60 µs, giving **2.33×** against LiteTopK, whereas the existing top-k v2 path gives **1.43×**.

These are cold-L2 CUDA-event timings, with 5 warmups and 40 measured iterations per implementation per round, 3 rounds with alternating order; table entries are medians of round medians. Inputs are already quantized; tensor generation and host scalar preparation are outside timing. Projection/quantization, KV-cache gathering, page-table conversion and the rest of attention are outside this operator benchmark, but included in serving TTFT. No CUDA graph is used in the operator benchmark. I covered 27 shapes total, including 32/64 heads and FP4 ratio 4 / k=1024. In this operator table, K=1024 and 1M=1,048,576 tokens.

### Serving TTFT (flag off → on)

Same pinned commit and checkpoint on both sides. The only runtime change is `SGLANG_OPT_USE_PREFILL_LITE_TOPK=0/1`. Each input is an identical, fixed-seed array of token IDs across the pair; prefix caching is disabled. One output token, temperature 0, `ignore_eos=true`. TTFT is measured at the arrival of the first streaming response reporting `completion_tokens > 0`, including single tokens whose UTF-8 text is not yet printable. Raw SSE metadata verifies the full requested prompt length, exactly one generated token, and zero cached tokens.

**Serving baseline detail:** the GLM TRT-LLM PAGED prefill configuration actually executes the legacy `topk_transform_prefill_kernel` with the flag off, confirmed in all eight rank profiles. At this commit, the CUDA top-k v2 prefill route handles RAGGED output, while the packed PAGED v2 route is ROCm-only. Therefore the GLM TTFT comparison is against its existing PAGED runtime path, **not against the top-k v2 operator microbenchmark above**. No top-k flag was forced off. See the pinned [runtime dispatch](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/599923b6f48d638d2256abbd0550c8fde141f4f5/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_topk_backend.py#L134-L215).

- GLM-5.2-FP8: checkpoint `f33c6dc501ee5a2c7e35155653b1b1abbc320951`, FP8 indexer (21 full-indexer layers out of 78), FP8 KV cache, TRT-LLM DSA prefill/decode and FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: checkpoint cache revision `5254448103b6254fc646dacbca1cbbf20e9216c1`, V4.1 KV layout, **FP4 compressed KV**, FlashMLA attention, FP8 sliding-window KV; only 3 layers execute full top-k.
- TP8 on two GB300 nodes, maximum 16,384-token prefill chunks, memory fraction 0.80, max 8 running requests, no speculation. Breakable prefill CUDA graphs enabled up to 16K sequence length; chunks with visible sequence length above 16K use eager prefill in both arms. Decode graph max batch size 8. `SGLANG_MOE_COPY_WEIGHT_VIEWS_BEFORE_H2D=1` in both arms.
- One full concurrent warmup wave for each shape, excluded. Concurrency 1: median of 8 measured requests. Concurrency 8: mean of 32 measured requests (closed-loop concurrency limit, including scheduler queueing). Compilation, model startup and separate dispatch-validation profiles are excluded.

**Concurrency 1 — TTFT in seconds**

| Input tokens | GLM-5.2-FP8 off → on | Speedup | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash off → on | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,192 | 0.284 → 0.284 | 0.998× | 0.081 → 0.081 | 1.002× |
| 16,384 | 0.555 → 0.553 | 1.004× | 0.134 → 0.133 | 1.004× |
| 32,768 | 1.150 → 1.120 | 1.027× | 0.255 → 0.249 | 1.024× |
| 65,536 | 2.445 → 2.296 | 1.065× | 0.801 → 0.800 | 1.001× |
| 131,072 | 5.593 → 4.822 | 1.160× | 1.694 → 1.716 | 0.987× |
| 262,144 | 14.795 → 10.605 | 1.395× | 3.577 → 3.587 | 0.997× |
| 524,288 | 43.404 → 25.409 | 1.708× | 7.079 → 7.159 | 0.989× |
| 1,000,000 | 129.569 → 63.325 | 2.046× | 14.067 → 13.571 | 1.037× |

**Concurrency 8 — TTFT in seconds**

| Input tokens | GLM-5.2-FP8 off → on | Speedup | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash off → on | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32,768 | 8.129 → 7.921 | 1.026× | 1.714 → 1.720 | 0.997× |
| 65,536 | 17.325 → 16.265 | 1.065× | 5.402 → 5.704 | 0.947× |
| 131,072 | 39.638 → 34.188 | 1.159× | 12.078 → 12.012 | 1.006× |
| 262,144 | 104.960 → 75.231 | 1.395× | 25.047 → 24.750 | 1.012× |

The longest serving input is **1,000,000 tokens** (not 1,048,576); the configured context limit is 1,048,576. These are synthetic-input performance measurements, not a model-accuracy benchmark. Runs were sequential off/on on exclusive nodes; small percentage differences should not be overinterpreted.

The FP4 model did not show a large or uniform TTFT gain in this sweep: ratios range from **0.947× to 1.037×**. The 64K / concurrency-8 case was **5.6% slower** with LiteTopK. This is one sequential off/on sweep, not a multi-run variance study. I would not use the small differences as evidence of a universal gain or regression. The serving model here is GLM-5.2 with FP8 weights; this is not a reproduction of the GLM NVFP4 checkpoint in the vLLM chart.

Separate 12-step prefill profiles confirm that all eight ranks execute the new indexer and candidate kernels with the flag on and none of those kernels with it off. Profiling and trace parsing are outside the TTFT measurements.

### JIT compilation

Each cold run uses a **new dedicated cache directory and a new process**, with Python imports and CUDA context creation outside the timer. A second new process reuses that directory with `SGLANG_CRASH_ON_JIT_COMPILE=1`, verifying disk-cache reuse. Three repetitions per variant; 72/72 cold/cache runs succeeded.

| Module / specialization | Cold compile + load, median (range), s | Disk-cache load, median, ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP8 indexer, 32 heads | 9.222 (9.120–9.295) | 27.5 |
| FP8 indexer, 64 heads | 9.190 (9.084–9.204) | 31.8 |
| FP4 indexer, 32 heads | 8.764 (8.498–8.784) | 32.8 |
| FP4 indexer, 64 heads | 8.460 (8.365–8.504) | 34.2 |
| Candidate top-k, FP32, k=512/1024/2048 | 6.32–6.37 (variant medians) | 26.9–30.8 |
| Candidate top-k, BF16, k=512/1024/2048 | 6.31–6.41 (variant medians) | 27.3–30.6 |
| Page-table transform, page64 / k2048 | 5.608 (5.478–5.618) | 24.8 |
| Existing top-k v2 factory, including occupancy probes | 35.816 (35.201–35.823) | 53.6 |

The indexer and candidate selector are separate JIT modules: the ~9 s indexer figure is **not** the whole cold first-request cost. For a typical FP8 specialization, the **sum of the separately measured cold module medians** is roughly 15.5 s, plus page-table transformation if needed; this sum is not a measured first-request latency. Short chunks still use the dense path, so enabling LiteTopK can require compiling both the baseline and the new modules; the comparison is not a claim of faster whole-server cold startup. Model loading, other kernels, CUDA graph capture, and process initialization are not part of these numbers.

### Validation / limits

- First generated token IDs agreed in 123/192 GLM request pairs and 163/192 DeepSeek request pairs. Deterministic inference mode was not enabled. Both models also had disagreements at 8K, below the LiteTopK dispatch threshold, so these run-level differences should not be attributed solely to LiteTopK. These synthetic-input performance measurements **do not establish model-accuracy equivalence**; all requests did pass prompt-length, one-output-token and zero-prefix-cache checks.
- All 45 tests in the four new attention test files passed. The 39 PR-changed files on the benchmark host match the pinned commit byte for byte.
- Across the 27 benchmark shapes: no negative/out-of-range output indices and no candidate overflow. First/last 16 query rows additionally had no duplicate/missing indices or selected scores below the dense cutoff beyond a relative 1e-5 tolerance; minimum exact-set recall was 0.9935 on BF16 ties. These checks are not a general exact-top-k guarantee or a model-accuracy evaluation.
- The operator ratios should not be read as model-level TTFT ratios or compared directly to the vLLM chart: the baseline selector, model/indexer layer frequency, GPU and serving configuration differ.

## Motivation

DSA-style sparse attention (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V4.1) picks the top-k keys of every prefill row from an indexer score over all visible keys. Today this is DeepGEMM `mqa_logits` writing the full `[rows, keys]` logits, then a separate top-k over them. At long context both the logits traffic and the top-k grow with `rows x keys`.

This PR adds an opt-in sampled-threshold path (after [LiteTopK](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976), building on #46434): one SM100 kernel scores every key on the tensor cores and keeps only the keys at or above a per-row threshold taken from a strided sample of the row's scores (about 2.25 x topk candidates per row), then a small top-k selects among the candidates. The logits are never written.

## Changes

- Kernels (`kernels/jit/csrc/dsa/litetopk_prefill/`): FP8 indexer (DSA, 32/64 index heads), FP4 indexer (DeepSeek-V4.1, 32/64 index heads), fp32 / bf16 candidate top-k (topk 512 / 1024 / 2048); `attention/topk_page_table_transform.cuh` maps request-relative positions to KV slots through the page-size-64 table (PAGED output).
- Ops: `attention.fp8_indexer_topk`, `attention.fp4_indexer_topk`, `attention.topk_page_table_transform_`.
- Integration behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_PREFILL_LITE_TOPK=1` (default off):
  - DSA prefill (RAGGED and PAGED / trtllm outputs) when the batch's longest row sees at least `8 x index_topk` keys.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1 full top-k layers when the batch's longest request has at least 24576 compressed keys.
  - Shorter batches keep the dense path.
- First commit: a refactor of the `sgl_kernel` PTX helpers into `sgl_kernel/ptx/{barrier,async,tcgen05}.cuh` (shared by the new kernels and the existing wo_a / kimi attn_res / hicache / muse kernels), plus packed fp32x2 math helpers.
- Requires nvcc >= 13.4 for the JIT kernels.

## Kernel performance (B300, cold L2, indexer + top-k, us; ratio = baseline / ours)

FP8, 32 heads, topk 2048 (single request, last rows), vs DeepGEMM fp8 logits + DeepSelect:

| context x rows | ours | DeepGEMM + DeepSelect | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32K x 4096 | 482 | 1181 | 2.45 |
| 128K x 4096 | 1533 | 3307 | 2.16 |
| 256K x 8192 | 5932 | 11733 | 1.98 |
| 1M x 4096 | 11881 | 18732 | 1.58 |
| 1M x 16384 | 50161 | 84329 | 1.68 |

FP4, DeepSeek-V4.1 shapes (compress ratio 2, topk 512), vs DeepGEMM bf16 logits + DeepSelect:

| context x rows | keys | ours | DG + DS | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64K x 4096 (32 heads) | 32K | 397 | 459 | 1.16 |
| 256K x 16384 (32 heads) | 128K | 5182 | 5919 | 1.14 |
| 1M x 16384 (32 heads) | 512K | 20078 | 22477 | 1.12 |
| 256K x 16384 (64 heads) | 128K | 9095 | 9380 | 1.03 |

Below ~16K keys the filter keeps most keys and DeepGEMM + top-k is as fast or faster, hence the routing thresholds above.

## End-to-end (GLM-5.3 FP8, 8x B300, cookbook TP8 + EAGLE, trtllm prefill)

| workload | off | on | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| single 128K request, TTFT | 6690 ms | 5837 ms | -12.7% |
| single 64K request, TTFT | 2929 ms | 2761 ms | -5.7% |
| 128K x concurrency 4, input tok/s | 19942 | 23436 | +17.5% |
| 8K / 16K single request | | | within noise |

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (4x B200 TP4/EP4; AgentX screens on B300): within noise, since only 3 layers use the full top-k indexer.

  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: 2.3M rows, mean recall 0.994; all disagreements are copies of the k-th value (bf16 ties).

  - GLM-5.3: ruler2 128K 87.27 / 87.69.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: gsm8k 96.66 / 96.89; ruler2 128K 82.17 / 79.68, paired difference not significant (p = 0.39).

+
+One launch scores every visible key of each query row (32 or 64 index heads
+x 128, e.g. GLM-5.2 / 5.3 with 32; fp8 index K with a per-key fp32 scale) on
+the tensor cores and keeps, per row, the keys whose score reaches a threshold set
+from a strided sample of the row's scores. The ``[rows, keys]`` logits are
+never written; the output is a per-row candidate slab for a separate top-k
+kernel. Kernel source: ``kernels/jit/csrc/dsa/litetopk_prefill/fp8_indexer.cuh``.

+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, NamedTuple, Optional

+    from tvm_ffi.module import Module

+FP8_INDEXER_HEAD_DIM = 128
+# Slab width: the real-data candidate maximum is ~10K per row (DESIGN.md).
+FP8_INDEXER_CAP = 12288
+# Pipeline depths: 3 x 32 KB KV stages (4 and 5 measured equal), 2 x 16 KB Q stages (the
+# third went to the 16 KB candidate staging).

+DEFAULT_Q_STAGES = 2

+def _num_sms(device: torch.device) -> int:
+    return torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).multi_processor_count

+    scores: torch.Tensor  # [rows, cap] fp32, unordered
+    indices: torch.Tensor  # [rows, cap] int32, key - ks[row]
+    counts: torch.Tensor  # [rows] int32, scores >= T (may exceed cap)
+    thresholds: torch.Tensor  # [rows] fp32
+    overflow: torch.Tensor  # [rows] int32, 1 when count > cap
+
+
+# Fixed cost of a scan unit (pipeline fill, block-end sync) in 256-key tiles; fitted on B200 (128K-1M keys,
+# 64-1024 rows).
+UNIT_OVERHEAD_TILES = 10
+

+def pick_tail_chunks(num_blocks: int, num_ctas: int, block_tiles: int) -> int:
+    """Pieces per block of the last, partial wave: the one of 1, 2, ..., 32 that ends the launch first. With grid =
+    min(num_ctas, num_blocks C), the full waves take num_blocks // grid block times and the tail of r blocks in C
+    pieces ceil(r C / grid) / C, plus UNIT_OVERHEAD_TILES / block_tiles per unit a CTA runs."""
+    unit_cost = UNIT_OVERHEAD_TILES / max(block_tiles, 1)
+
+    def launch_time(c: int) -> float:
+        grid = min(num_ctas, num_blocks * c)
+        tail = num_blocks % grid
+        units = -(-tail * c // grid)
+        return num_blocks // grid * (1 + unit_cost) + (
+            units / c + units * unit_cost if tail else 0.0
+        )
+
+    return min((1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), key=launch_time)

+_SAMPLE_CODES: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None

+    """int32 scratch of the scan pieces (zero between launches; every launch leaves it zero)."""

+def fp8_indexer_candidates(

+    weights: torch.Tensor,

+            counts=torch.empty((rows,), dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+            thresholds=torch.empty((rows,), dtype=torch.float32, device=device),
+            overflow=torch.empty((rows,), dtype=torch.int32, device=device),

+        weights,
+        kv_fp8,
+        kv_scale,

+        ke,

+        _sample_codes(q_fp8.device),
+        out.scores,

+"""The fp4 DSA prefill indexer (candidate slab) against today's path, DeepGEMM bf16 logits

+

+from sglang.kernels.jit.benchmark import marker

+
+def make_inputs(heads, rows, ctx, ratio):
+    from deep_gemm.utils.math import per_token_cast_to_fp4
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    num_kv = ctx // ratio
+    pos = torch.arange(ctx - rows, ctx, device="cuda")
+    ks = torch.zeros(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    ke = ((pos + 1) // ratio).to(torch.int32)
+    q = torch.randn(rows, heads, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    kv = torch.randn(num_kv, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    weights = torch.randn(rows, heads, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    q_fp4, q_sf = per_token_cast_to_fp4(
+        q.view(-1, 128), use_ue8m0=True, gran_k=32, use_packed_ue8m0=True
+    )
+    kv_fp4, kv_sf = per_token_cast_to_fp4(
+        kv, use_ue8m0=True, gran_k=32, use_packed_ue8m0=True
+    )
+    return (
+        q_fp4.view(rows, heads, 64).contiguous(),
+        q_sf.view(rows, heads).contiguous(),
+        weights,
+        kv_fp4.contiguous(),
+        kv_sf.view(-1).contiguous(),
+        ks,
+        ke,
+    )
+
+
+def ours(q_fp4, q_sf, weights, kv_fp4, kv_sf, ks, ke, topk):
+    return fp4_indexer_candidates(
+        q_fp4, q_sf, weights, kv_fp4, kv_sf, ks, ke, topk
+    ).scores
+
+
+def deep_gemm_deep_select(q_fp4, q_sf, weights, kv_fp4, kv_sf, ks, ke, topk):
+    from deep_gemm import fp8_fp4_mqa_logits
+
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.deep_select import topk as ds_topk
+
+    rows = q_fp4.shape[0]
+    width = (int((ke - ks).max()) + 63) // 64 * 64
+    logits = fp8_fp4_mqa_logits(

+        (kv_fp4, kv_sf),

+HEADS = (32, 64)

+CAP = 12288

+# from the block's span, at most MAX_SAMPLE_TILES tiles of 256.

+    return 65 if span <= 524288 else 129 if span <= 1048576 else 257

+    requests: Sequence[Tuple[int, int, str]], device="cuda"

+    request b at positions p see keys [cum_b, cum_b + p + 1) (sglang ragged
+    prefill convention). Returns ks, ke (int32) and the key count."""
+    ks: List[int] = []
+    ke: List[int] = []
+    cum = 0
+    for ctx, rows, where in requests:
+        assert rows <= ctx

+        for p in range(first, first + rows):
+            ks.append(cum)
+            ke.append(cum + p + 1)
+        cum += ctx

+        torch.tensor(ks, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        torch.tensor(ke, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),

+and ``dsa/litetopk_prefill/topk_candidates_bf16.cuh``, both behind ``topk_candidates``).
+
+Rows are synthetic candidate slabs: a long score row, a threshold T taken as the
+fp16 floor of the (1 + alpha) k-th largest score, the candidates ``>= T`` in key
+order. The exact fp32 top-k set must come back (ties at the k-th value may be
+swapped), ``-1`` exactly past ``min(k, count)``.

+import sys

+import pytest
+import torch

+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.litetopk_prefill.topk_candidates import (

+)

+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+INT_MAX = 2**31 - 1
+
+

+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 10:
+        pytest.skip(

+        )

+def make_rows(rows, k, counts, gen, cap=TOPK_CANDIDATES_CAP, thr_mode="band"):
+    """Slab rows with the given candidate counts; scores ~ N(-60, 5) like GLM logits."""
+    scores = torch.full((rows, cap), -float("inf"), device="cuda")
+    indices = torch.full((rows, cap), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    thr = torch.empty(rows, device="cuda")
+    for r in range(rows):
+        n = int(counts[r])
+        s = torch.randn(n, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 5 - 60
+        if thr_mode == "band" and n > 0:
+            t = s.min().half().float()  # fp16-representable, <= every candidate
+        else:  # "neg_inf"
+            t = -float("inf")
+        scores[r, :n] = s
+        indices[r, :n] = torch.sort(
+            torch.randperm(1 << 20, device="cuda", generator=gen)[:n]
+        ).values.to(torch.int32)
+        thr[r] = t
+    count = torch.tensor(counts, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

+
+def positions_of(indices, count, sel, valid):
+    """Key indices -> positions in the live prefix of each row (-1 when absent)."""
+    R, C = indices.shape
+    live = torch.arange(C, device=sel.device)[None, :] < count[:, None]
+    pad = torch.where(live, indices, torch.full_like(indices, INT_MAX))
+    sorted_idx, perm = pad.sort(dim=1)
+    q = torch.where(valid, sel, torch.zeros_like(sel))
+    loc = torch.searchsorted(sorted_idx, q.contiguous()).clamp(max=C - 1)
+    found = (sorted_idx.gather(1, loc) == q) & valid
+    return torch.where(found, perm.gather(1, loc), torch.full_like(loc, -1))
+

+def check(scores, indices, count, k, out):
+    """Tie-aware exactness: the selected scores, sorted, equal the exact top-k scores, sorted."""
+    R, C = scores.shape

+    valid = col < n[:, None]

+        scores.gather(1, pos.clamp(min=0)),
+        torch.full_like(pos, 0, dtype=scores.dtype) - float("inf"),

+    slot = torch.arange(indices.shape[1], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")[None, :]

+    )

+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    if off is not None:

+    s[k - 100 : k + 100 : 2] = -0.0

**1. Sample single keys instead of 8-key blocks (the important one).** Top keys sit in runs, so an 8-key block either lands in one or misses it, and Threshold gets noisy. At 1,000,000 input tokens / concurrency 1, GLM-5.2-FP8 TTFT is **129.57 → 63.33 s (2.046×, 51.1% lower)**. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is **14.07 → 13.57 s (1.037×)**. The FP8 indexer module takes about **9.2 s** to compile/load cold; the separate cold medians for indexer plus candidate selector sum to about **15.5 s**, excluding other startup work.

### Environment and comparison

- 8× NVIDIA GB300 (SM103), two exclusive 4-GPU nodes. Kernel/JIT measurements use one GPU; serving uses TP8 across both nodes. GPU clocks were not locked by this benchmark.
- Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, nvcc/CUDA runtime headers 13.4.92, driver 590.48.01; FlashInfer 0.7.2, DeepGEMM 0.2.3.post2, sgl-kernel 0.4.10, TVM FFI 0.1.11. `MAX_JOBS=8`.
- For the **operator microbenchmarks**, the FP8 baseline is **DeepGEMM + the existing top-k v2**, not only DeepSelect; the FP4 baseline is DeepGEMM BF16 logits + DeepSelect. Both include score generation and selection. Serving uses the actual runtime dispatch described below.

### Complete indexer + top-k

32 index heads, 4,096 query rows (last causal chunk), head dimension 128. FP8: k=2048. FP4: k=512, compression ratio 2, so the number of keys is half the original context length. Times below are microseconds; speedup = baseline / LiteTopK.

| 32K | 656.00 → 457.34 | 1.43× | 234.14 → 215.74 | 1.09× |

| 1M | 19783.33 → 12409.54 | 1.59× | 5481.12 → 4881.06 | 1.12× |

At 1M context / 16,384 query rows, FP8 is **79.62 → 49.59 ms (1.61×)** and FP4 is **21.14 → 18.90 ms (1.12×)**. The direct FP8 op is slower at 8K, but the production dispatch guard excludes that shape.

Baseline choice matters: for FP8 32K × 4096, DeepGEMM + DeepSelect takes 1065.60 µs, giving **2.33×** against LiteTopK, whereas the existing top-k v2 path gives **1.43×**.

These are cold-L2 CUDA-event timings, with 5 warmups and 40 measured iterations per implementation per round, 3 rounds with alternating order; table entries are medians of round medians. Inputs are already quantized; tensor generation and host scalar preparation are outside timing. Projection/quantization, KV-cache gathering, page-table conversion and the rest of attention are outside this operator benchmark, but included in serving TTFT. No CUDA graph is used in the operator benchmark. I covered 27 shapes total, including 32/64 heads and FP4 ratio 4 / k=1024. In this operator table, K=1024 and 1M=1,048,576 tokens.

Same pinned commit and checkpoint on both sides. The only runtime change is `SGLANG_OPT_USE_PREFILL_LITE_TOPK=0/1`. At this commit, the CUDA top-k v2 prefill route handles RAGGED output, while the packed PAGED v2 route is ROCm-only.
